filename: MONITORING ACCESS TO PIPED WATER AND SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE IN AFRICA AT DISAGGREGATED SCALES USING SATELLITE IMAGERY AND SELFSUPERVISED LEARNING.pdf
title: MONITORING ACCESS TO PIPED WATER AND SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE IN AFRICA AT DISAGGREGATED SCALES USING SATELLITE IMAGERY AND SELF-SUPERVISED LEARNING
venue: ICLR 2026 Machine Learning for Remote Sensing (ML4RS) Workshop
testbed_rationale: This paper evaluates satellite imagery classification using self-supervised foundation models to monitor water and sanitation infrastructure access (SDG 6), which is not a physical climate/earth system parameterization or numerical model testbed.
pain_points: Indirect observability: water networks and sewage infrastructure are not directly visible in optical imagery, forcing models to rely on settlement proxies.
Indicator definition mismatch between household survey binary questions and official WHO/UNICEF JMP service categories.
Spatial and temporal distribution shifts when generalizing to unsampled regions and countries without survey data.
Heterogeneous ground truth coverage and sample density across survey rounds.
extraction_notes: The paper is a workshop paper accepted at the ICLR 2026 ML4RS workshop. Pretraining and fine-tuning involved ViT models including DINOv1, DINOv2, DINOv3, Galileo, and Prithvi-EO-2.0.
